explanation.explanation_en: The usual collocation is 'make a decision' (British English also allows 'take a decision'). We 'make' decisions, plans and mistakes, but we 'do' tasks. Past simple 'made' is used because 'last week' is a finished past time.
explanation.explanation_vi: Cụm từ thông dụng là 'make a decision' (ra quyết định; tiếng Anh-Anh cũng nói 'take a decision'). Ta 'make' decisions, plans, mistakes, nhưng 'do' tasks. Vì 'last week' là thời gian quá khứ đã kết thúc nên dùng quá khứ đơn 'made'.

body.prompt: Choose the correct word to complete the collocation: After the long meeting, everyone finally ___ a decision.

_provenance.cefr_reasoning: The item tests the basic collocation 'make a decision' with simple past tense and everyday vocabulary. 'Make vs do' collocations are typically introduced at A2, and the sentence structure is a simple past sentence well below B1 complexity.

explanation.explanation_en: The correct collocation is 'make a decision'. In English, we 'make' decisions, plans, and mistakes, but we 'do' work or tasks.
explanation.explanation_vi: Cụm từ đúng là 'make a decision'. Trong tiếng Anh, ta dùng 'make' với decision, plan, mistake, nhưng dùng 'do' với work hoặc task.

examples.note: Verb + noun collocations: 'make progress' (not 'do progress') and 'take notes' (not 'write notes' in this common fixed phrase).
examples.text: We made good progress in the meeting, and the manager took notes carefully.

examples.note: Adjective + noun ('heavy traffic', not 'strong traffic') and adverb + verb ('completely miss') show how collocations combine naturally in one sentence.
examples.text: The heavy traffic made us completely miss the beginning of the film.

examples.note: Adverb + verb collocation: 'strongly recommend' is the natural pairing; 'very recommend' is incorrect.
examples.text: I strongly recommend doing this exercise — it's a great way to improve your vocabulary.

body.objective: Understand what collocations are and master common high-frequency verb + noun, adjective + noun, and adverb + adjective collocations at CEFR B1 level, so learners can produce natural word combinations instead of literal translations.

explanation.en: A collocation is a natural combination of two or more words that frequently appear together, e.g. 'make a decision', 'heavy rain', 'strong coffee'. Collocations are not governed by strict grammar rules; they are conventions of usage learned through exposure. Key types at B1 level include: (1) verb + noun: do homework, take a photo, make progress, have a shower; (2) adjective + noun: fast food, deep sleep, close friend, heavy traffic; (3) adverb + adjective: completely different, highly successful, deeply concerned; (4) adverb + verb: strongly recommend, badly damage. Important principles: verbs like 'do', 'make', 'take', 'have', and 'get' combine with specific nouns and cannot be swapped freely — we 'make a mistake' but 'do a mistake' is wrong. Adjectives also pair selectively: we say 'heavy rain' not 'strong rain', and 'strong coffee' not 'heavy coffee'. Learning words in chunks rather than in isolation improves fluency, accuracy, and naturalness. When in doubt, check a collocations dictionary or notice combinations in authentic reading and listening texts.
explanation.vi: Collocation (kết hợp từ) là cách các từ thường đi cùng nhau một cách tự nhiên trong tiếng Anh, ví dụ 'make a decision' (quyết định), 'heavy rain' (mưa lớn). Đây không phải quy tắc ngữ pháp cứng nhắc mà là thói quen dùng từ của người bản xứ, nên người học Việt Nam rất dễ dịch sát nghĩa và nói sai. Các dạng quan trọng ở trình độ B1: (1) động từ + danh từ: do homework, take a photo, make progress, have a shower; (2) tính từ + danh từ: fast food, deep sleep, heavy traffic; (3) trạng từ + tính từ: completely different, highly successful; (4) trạng từ + động từ: strongly recommend. Lưu ý các động từ 'do, make, take, have, get' đi với danh từ cố định: ta nói 'make a mistake' chứ không 'do a mistake'; 'heavy rain' chứ không 'strong rain'. Cách học hiệu quả nhất là học cả cụm từ thay vì học từng từ rời rạc, và ghi chú collocation gặp được khi đọc, nghe.

common_mistakes.why: The noun 'mistake' collocates with 'make', not 'do'. Vietnamese learners often translate 'làm lỗi' literally as 'do a mistake', but English fixes this pairing: make a mistake, make an error, make a decision.
common_mistakes.right: I made a big mistake in the exam.
common_mistakes.wrong: I did a big mistake in the exam.

common_mistakes.why: 'Rain' collocates with 'heavy' (heavy rain, heavy snow), while 'strong' pairs with coffee, wind, smell, and opinion. Each adjective has its own set of natural noun partners.
common_mistakes.right: There was heavy rain all day, so we stayed at home.
common_mistakes.wrong: There was strong rain all day, so we stayed at home.
